stem: Brown has six fewer cubes than gray. How many are on gray?

stem: White has this many fewer cubes than pink. How many are on white?

Mark that span at the end of the longer bar. | Shape: Derive the grouped larger total and find the smaller with fewer. Reserve the pink groups and the two difference pieces. Match the whole difference to the uncovered end. Practice adjusts a supplied model.
samples: Shown: 11 − 4 = 7 on white. | Not yet seen: 4 on white (error J).

stem: Black has one more cube than tan. How many are on tan?

Descriptive evidence. | Shape: reconstruct the smaller tray from a grouped larger referent and more language. Reserve source groups and difference together. Practice explains a different given comparison.
samples: Shown: ? + 1 = 12. 11 on tan. | Not yet seen: 13 from more (error H).

stem: What length belongs on the short strip's tag?

stem: What length belongs on the long strip's tag?
answer: 16 units.

stem: How many more units does the short strip need to reach the end of the long strip?

Align starts and link the short strip and its five-unit extension to the long strip. | Shape: determine the extension from the two physically measured lengths, with a model linked to an equation. Reserve this strip pair, marks and question. Practice places given lengths into other bars or checks supplied labels.
samples: Shown: 5 more units. 11 + 5 = 16 or 16 − 11 = 5. | Not yet seen: 16 more units (error J).

answer: 2 small pieces.

stem: What is ten more than 94?

stem: What is 61 + 27?
What is ten more than 93?

steps: Invented for practice. Children mark the join.

stem: Rin adds 2 units to a strip of 4. How long is it now?
steps: Invented for practice. Use a paper strip and two matching pieces, then draw three moments.

stem: How many cubes stick out when we match 6 with 4?

stem: Rin takes 3 pieces away. Five are left. How many were there first?
steps: Invented for practice. Restore three, then name the starting amount.

stem: One strip is 8 units long, 2 fewer than another. How long is the other?
answer: 10 units.

stem: A 12-unit strip is 2 units longer than another. How long is the other?
answer: 10 units.
steps: Invented for practice. Cover the extra two along the long bar.

stem: Rin adds two paper leaves to six. How many are there now?
answer: 8 leaves.
steps: Invented for practice. Show the before and after groups on a blank mat.

stem: A paper fox trail is nine units long. A paper hare trail is two units shorter. How long is the hare trail?
answer: 7 units.

stem: A tray holds 12 cards. Five are circles. How many are triangles?
answer: 7 triangles.
steps: Invented for practice. Use familiar practice after the transfer and assessment revisions.

stem: Circle the solids whose outsides are flat everywhere.
answer: The cube and the noncube rectangular prism only.
steps: Both have flat faces throughout. The cone and cylinder each have a curved surface. | Shape: select all members of the four-solid feature group. Reserve models, views and card. Practice uncovers a partner's hidden rule with other objects.
samples: Shown: The cube and the noncube rectangular prism only. | Not yet seen: Circles the red cube and red cone because both are red. (error A)

stem: Show what makes each circled solid belong.
answer: Marks flat faces on both chosen solids.
steps: Accept tracing or pointing at flat faces on the matching paper views. No spoken word is required. | Shape: annotate the basis of one's own grouping. Practice feels or traces one indicated surface on one solid.
samples: Shown: Marks flat faces on both chosen solids. | Not yet seen: Marks only the largest solid because of its size. (error A)

stem: Draw a cylinder joined to this build.
answer: A cylinder touches the outlined cube-prism build.
steps: Keep the cube and rectangular prism in their original contact. | Shape: extend a pictured starting build independently. Practice turns a different real pair as one. Reserve cube, prism, joint and cylinder together.
samples: Shown: A cylinder touches the outlined cube-prism build. | Not yet seen: Separates the cube and prism to insert the cylinder. (error D)

stem: Trace the first build inside your new one.
answer: Traces around the original joined cube and prism together.
steps: The trace includes both initial solids and leaves the added cylinder outside. | Shape: recover a specified first build from one's own extended drawing. Practice sketches separate parts or the outer silhouette of a different build.
samples: Shown: Traces around the original joined cube and prism together. | Not yet seen: Traces two separate solids after pulling the first build apart. (error D)

stem: What shapes are in your build?
answer: Cube, rectangular prism, cylinder.
steps: Cover the picture labels until the child responds. Accept the names or plain word labels read aloud in mixed order. Use the pictures for feedback or record a picture-supported response as shown with help. Score the names separately from the join. | Shape: label the three component solids in the finished build. Practice labels a cylinder-and-cone sketch.
samples: Shown: Cube, rectangular prism, cylinder. | Shown with help: Matches all three pictures after the first attempt. | Not yet seen: Names the cylinder as a cone.

stem: Circle shapes that belong together because of their sides.
answer: Both triangles for three straight sides, or both triangles and the square for only straight sides.
steps: Credit another consistent side rule only if the group includes all and only its members. | Shape: select membership across a new quartet. Practice tests a supplied rule on one piece at a time. Reserve all four outlines and their orientations.
samples: Shown: Both triangles for three straight sides, or both triangles and the square for only straight sides. | Not yet seen: Circles only the upright triangle because the other is turned. (error A)

stem: What is your side rule?
answer: Three straight sides, only straight sides, or another matching side rule.
steps: Accept a picture mark of the shared feature or neutral transcription. A word omission alone does not undo a correct mark. | Shape: supply the geometric rule for one's own group. Practice corrects a supplied label on a single card.
samples: Shown: Three straight sides, only straight sides, or another matching side rule. | Not yet seen: Gives the shapes' color as the side rule. (error A)

stem: Draw a closed shape with four straight sides.
answer: Any simple closed quadrilateral.
steps: Allow intended straight joins and minor motor imprecision. Describe a deliberately open join without a letter. | Shape: create the complete figure on empty dot paper. Practice completes a partially drawn outline with another side count.
samples: Shown: Any simple closed quadrilateral. | Not yet seen: Draws a large circle because size makes it fit. (error A)

stem: Mark the sides.
answer: One mark on each of the four sides.
steps: Check that each edge has a single visible mark. Record number or location slips descriptively. | Shape: annotate the sides on one's own figure. Practice feels and counts a hidden piece.
samples: Shown: One mark on each of the four sides. | Not yet seen: Marks only the corner points.

stem: Dot the corners.
answer: A dot at each of four corners.
steps: Check the joins of the child’s outline. An adult may transfer the child’s exact indicated locations. | Shape: mark corners on one's own completed outline. Practice handles a supplied shape.
samples: Shown: A dot at each of four corners. | Not yet seen: Dots the centers of the edges.

stem: Draw a skinny triangle.
answer: A narrow closed outline with three straight sides.
steps: Accept any intentional skinny triangle. | Shape: draw an unstarted skinny example. Practice tests a supplied edge. Reserve this mat.
samples: Shown: A narrow closed outline with three straight sides. | Not yet seen: Leaves a corner open and accepts the figure as a triangle. (error B)

stem: Draw a turned triangle.
answer: A closed three-straight-sided triangle turned from the first.
steps: Accept any perceptibly different orientation. | Shape: produce a second triangle on a blank companion mat. Practice moves a finished piece.
samples: Shown: A closed three-straight-sided triangle turned from the first. | Not yet seen: Draws a bowed side and treats it as straight. (error C)

stem: Mark what both triangles need.
answer: Marks the closed joins and the three straight sides of both drawings.
steps: Read the paired paper marks or record an exact pointing response on that paper. | Shape: show the shared essentials on a child's paired drawings. Keep this paired layout out of practice.
samples: Shown: Marks the closed joins and the three straight sides of both drawings. | Not yet seen: Marks only the color.

stem: Show something that can change.
answer: Indicates a different turn, size or color.
steps: Accept a small sketch or a one-word label. Both remain triangles. | Shape: identify variation on the child's paired drawings. Practice checks an existing edge or open join.
samples: Shown: Indicates a different turn, size or color. | Not yet seen: Crosses out the turned drawing because it cannot be a triangle. (error A)

stem: Mark every rectangle.
answer: Marks the first four drawings and omits the slanted fifth.
steps: Each chosen drawing has four straight sides and four square corners. | Shape: select a four-member family from five fresh drawings. Practice checks one corner with a folded guide.
samples: Shown: Marks the first four drawings and omits the slanted fifth. | Not yet seen: Leaves out the recolored rectangle because of its color. (error A)

stem: Why is the turned one still a rectangle?
answer: Four straight sides meet at four square corners.
steps: Accept marking the four square corners or indicating how a paper corner fits them. | Shape: explain membership across the reserved family. Practice tests single shapes and individual changes.
samples: Shown: Four straight sides meet at four square corners. | Not yet seen: Says it stays a rectangle because it is still the same color. (error A)

stem: Join these two pieces into a circle.
answer: The matching half-circles touch along their full straight edges.
steps: The outer edge makes one complete circle. Use a paper mark showing the seam of the child’s build. | Shape: independently reconstruct a circle from the given pair. Practice copies designs with other pieces. Reserve both half-circles and the rectangle in E135b.
samples: Shown: The matching half-circles touch along their full straight edges. | Not yet seen: Joins the curved edges so the outside is not a circle.

stem: Join your whole circle to this rectangle.
answer: An intact circle touches the rectangle in the larger design.
steps: Both halves remain joined. A tracing or paper tabs keep the full circle boundary visible. | Shape: reuse the child's first circle intact in the larger design. Practice copies an adult-started design with other shapes.
samples: Shown: An intact circle touches the rectangle in the larger design. | Not yet seen: Splits the half-circles across the rectangle. (error D)

stem: Trace what makes this whole a circle.
answer: Traces the entire round outer boundary of the embedded circle.
steps: Ignore the straight internal seam. Accept neutral support to trace where the child indicates. | Shape: annotate the circle embedded in the child's design. Practice checks an isolated curve.
samples: Shown: Traces the entire round outer boundary of the embedded circle. | Not yet seen: Uses the circle’s color as the deciding feature. (error A)

stem: Add one piece to this flat whole.
answer: Adds one touching piece to the band-and-panel square.
steps: Its two unequal rectangles and off-center seam remain unchanged. | Shape: extend the supplied band-and-panel square independently. Reserve its parts and joint. Practice verifies the seam in a supplied trapezoid-and-triangle image.
samples: Shown: Adds one touching piece to the band-and-panel square. | Not yet seen: Separates the two rectangles to place the new piece between them. (error D)

stem: Add one piece to this solid whole.
answer: Adds one touching solid to the original two joined cubes.
steps: The cubes still share their original face. | Shape: preserve this connected solid pair in an extended drawing. Practice turns different solids.
samples: Shown: Adds one touching solid to the original two joined cubes. | Not yet seen: Separates the cubes to add the third solid. (error D)

stem: Mark a feature that makes it a square.
answer: Marks four equal straight sides or four square corners on the original square.

samples: Shown: Marks four equal straight sides or four square corners on the original square. | Not yet seen: Marks the fill and gives color as the deciding feature. (error A)

stem: Mark the pictures that show equal shares.
answer: Marks the stair-step circle and the rectangle with four equal strips only.

samples: Shown: Marks the stair-step circle and the rectangle with four equal strips only. | Not yet seen: Marks the off-center cap and remainder as equal. (error E)

stem: Where should this line go to make the shares equal?
answer: Draws a straight line across the circle through its center.

samples: Shown: Draws a straight line across the circle through its center. | Not yet seen: Redraws the off-center chord and calls its shares equal. (error E)

samples: Shown: Midway between the two solid dividers. | Not yet seen: Leaves the uneven dividers and calls the four strips equal. (error E)

stem: Label one share of this rectangle.

stem: Label one share of this circle.
answer: A fourth of or a quarter of the circle.

samples: Shown: A fourth of or a quarter of the circle. | Not yet seen: Labels one of the four existing sectors as a half.

stem: How many like this make the rectangle?

samples: Shown: Two halves. | Not yet seen: Marks 4 because the drawn band has four corners.

answer: Four fourths or four quarters.

samples: Shown: Four fourths or four quarters. | Not yet seen: Marks 2 because only one mark and one other piece are needed.

stem: Which starred circle piece is smaller?
answer: The starred fourth of the circle.

samples: Shown: The starred fourth of the circle. | Not yet seen: Marks the half as smaller because two is less than four. (error I)

stem: Which starred rectangle piece is smaller?
answer: The starred fourth of the rectangle.
steps: Compare only the starred horizontal bands of the matching rectangles. | Shape: compare the starred bands on two matching rectangle pictures. Reserve these bands and marks. Practice overlays loose pieces.
samples: Shown: The starred fourth of the rectangle. | Not yet seen: Marks the half as smaller because fewer equal shares make smaller pieces. (error I)

File as descriptive first-teaching evidence. | Shape: explain the difference on the intact circle pair. Practice covers a detached half and checks the fit without writing on a paired whole.
samples: Shown: Shows that the starred half splits into two equal fourths of the same-sized circle. | Not yet seen: Says a fourth is larger because four is more than two. (error I)

stem: Label one piece of this rectangle.
answer: A quarter of or a fourth of the rectangle.
steps: One of the four equal cells has the chosen label. | Shape: name a share on a cross-divided rectangle. Practice restores a missing loose piece.
samples: Shown: A quarter of or a fourth of the rectangle. | Not yet seen: Gives a whole-shape name and no share name.

stem: Which marked piece is smaller?
answer: The marked quarter in the cross-divided rectangle.

samples: Shown: The marked quarter in the cross-divided rectangle. | Not yet seen: Marks the half because fewer equal pieces must be smaller. (error I)

stem: Mark the hour hand.

stem: What time does the clock show?
answer: Four o’clock.

samples: Shown: Four o’clock. | Not yet seen: Says twelve o’clock from the long hand. (error G)

stem: Draw the hands for half past five.
answer: Long hand at 6 and short hand halfway between 5 and 6.

samples: Shown: Long hand at 6 and short hand halfway between 5 and 6. | Not yet seen: Draws the short hand right on 5. (error F)

stem: Show why the short hand belongs there.
answer: Marks halfway from 5 to 6 or shows that half the hour has passed.

samples: Shown: Marks halfway from 5 to 6 or shows that half the hour has passed. | Not yet seen: Leaves the hour hand fixed on 5 through the half hour. (error F)

answer: Short hand to hour, long hand to minute.

samples: Shown: Short hand to hour, long hand to minute. | Not yet seen: Links the long hand to hour. (error G)

stem: Write the time.
steps: The long hand shows the half hour. The short hand has passed 6 and has not reached 7. | Shape: derive digits from the full reserved 6:30 face. Practice starts from a digit card or fills a partial clock annotation.
samples: Shown: 6:30. | Not yet seen: Writes 6:06 from the numeral below the long hand. (error H)

stem: Draw the clock for art.
answer: Long hand at 6 and short hand halfway from 2 to 3.
steps: The complete drawing translates the stated event time. | Shape: translate the reserved event digits into a complete clock drawing on an empty face. Practice fixes a supplied hand.
samples: Shown: Long hand at 6 and short hand halfway from 2 to 3. | Not yet seen: Puts the short hand exactly at 2. (error F)

stem: Write the assembly time in digits.
steps: The short hand at 3 names the hour. The long hand at 12 means :00. | Shape: translate a second reserved event picture into digits with no supplied writing. Practice checks one hand on a different event card.
samples: Shown: 3:00. | Not yet seen: Writes 12:00 using the minute hand as the hour hand. (error G)

stem: Draw a copy of this joined piece.

samples: Shown: A second intact offset pair of equal squares. | Not yet seen: Draws the copied squares apart. (error D)

stem: How many squares are there altogether?
answer: 4 squares.

samples: Shown: 4 squares. | Not yet seen: Counts one joined pair as one square.

samples: Shown: 12:30. | Not yet seen: Writes 12:06, using the dial numeral as elapsed minutes. (error H)

stem: Which one is a triangle?
answer: The first, closed scalene triangle only.

samples: Shown: Marks three straight sides that meet to close the outline. | Not yet seen: Counts a curved mark as a straight side. (error C)

samples: Shown: Changes color with one stroke and retains the triangle. | Not yet seen: Says changing its color stops it being a triangle. (error A)

samples: Shown: A smaller closed three-straight-sided outline on the loose card. | Not yet seen: Says a smaller copy cannot be a triangle. (error A)

stem: Mark all the rectangles.
